notes: Genre envelopes used for premise, cast, scene and audit guidance. Conventions are craft constraints, not imitation targets. v2 adds roles, settings, pressures and antagonist_answers used by the deterministic premise, cast and scene generators.

fantasy.label: Fantasy
conventions: A secondary world with stated rules
A cost for power that shapes choices
A social order the protagonist must move through
A map of obligation, not decoration
fantasy.reader_promise: Wonder plus consequence: the impossible must obey rules that hurt someone.
pitfalls: Chosen-one framing with no earned competence
conflicts: the price of power against the ordinary good
fantasy.content_notes: Inherited fantasy tropes are fine; do not reproduce a specific living author's world or named characters.
settings: a river town that floods on the same day each year
a border keep with one gate and two masters
a market that only opens at low tide
a monastery library built over a well
pressures: the tithe is due and the harvest failed
the old road is closed by a law nobody remembers passing
the heir has not spoken in a year
a border treaty expires in nine days
antagonist_answers: order is worth more than any one life
power should belong to those who can carry its cost
the old law protects us from something worse

science-fiction.label: Science Fiction
conventions: One disciplined speculative premise
Consequences traced through ordinary institutions
Technology that redistributes power unevenly
A human question the science makes urgent
science-fiction.reader_promise: Cognitive estrangement: the reader's own world becomes visible through a changed one.
pitfalls: Handwaved physics that solves the plot
Metaphor that erases the actual science
science-fiction.content_notes: Avoid real classified programs, real persons, and current operational security detail.
roles: shift engineer on a water processor
archivist of a failing seed vault
freight pilot with a revoked medical licence
settings: a station whose air is rationed by algorithm
a terraforming site nineteen years behind schedule
a decommissioned orbital hospice
a city built inside a drained reservoir
pressures: the model that runs the district has started refusing requests
the generation ship is four bodies over capacity
a signal repeats from a source that should not exist
the licence to breathe is up for renewal
antagonist_answers: efficiency is the only honest ethics
a system that keeps ninety percent alive is just
intelligence without a body cannot be trusted

mystery.label: Mystery
conventions: A fair-play clue chain
A detective with a specific method
A closed set of suspects with motive, means, opportunity
A revelation that re-reads earlier scenes
mystery.reader_promise: Fair play: every solution element is on the page before the answer.
pitfalls: Withheld evidence the detective never sees
mystery.content_notes: Do not reproduce a real unsolved crime or real victim details.
settings: a hotel with one corridor of off-book rooms
a courthouse annex above a shuttered arcade
a harbour town where everyone knows the tide tables
a ninety-year-old printing house
pressures: a witness has changed one detail three times
the ledger balances only if two people are lying
a body is found where the map says water
an alibi depends on a clock that was reset
antagonist_answers: the record is the only innocent party
everyone with a motive is a victim of something else
the truth costs more than the lie

romance.label: Romance
conventions: A central relationship with a credible obstacle
Mutual agency in every escalation
An emotional beat map of attraction, rupture, and repair
An ending that affirms the relationship
romance.reader_promise: Emotional safety plus earned intimacy: the obstacle must be internal as well as external.
pitfalls: One character with no want of their own
conflicts: fear of being known against need
romance.content_notes: Keep all intimacy consensual and age-appropriate for the target audience.
settings: a shop that shares a wall with the person you cannot avoid
a wedding venue in the off-season
a ferry crossing twice a day
a flat above the family business
pressures: the business fails in six weeks unless one of them sells
one of them is leaving in the spring and has not said so
their families have a standing feud with a real cause
the paperwork requires them to work together daily
antagonist_answers: love should never require someone to shrink
loyalty to family is the same as love
wanting more is a kind of betrayal

horror.label: Horror
conventions: A threat with clear rules and a rising price
Dread built through anticipation, not gore
Isolation that is social as well as physical
An ending that leaves a stain
horror.reader_promise: Managed dread: the reader must be able to describe the threat's rules to a friend.
pitfalls: Characters making choices only to serve the plot
horror.content_notes: Graphic violence must be flagged in the brief's content limits; never target a real group.
settings: a care home with a wing that appears on no plan
a reservoir village exposed by drought
a tunnel with a light that answers
a house that is colder upstairs
pressures: the same child is drawn on three walls of different rooms
the recordings contain a voice from the room after everyone left
the tide now reaches the cellar door each night
the neighbours have all stopped answering
antagonist_answers: if we do not name it, it cannot take hold
survival is the only moral obligation
the dead deserve what the living refuse them

thriller.label: Thriller
conventions: A clock the protagonist cannot stop
An antagonist with initiative
Competence under pressure
Reversals driven by new information
thriller.reader_promise: Controlled acceleration: every chapter must shorten the distance to consequence.
thriller.content_notes: Do not depict operational detail for real weapons, explosives, or attacks.
settings: a container port at shift change
a hospital with one unlocked service door
a border crossing at 03:00
a call centre floor of four hundred desks
pressures: the deadline is in eleven hours and the file is already public
the witness they must protect has stopped trusting them
the wrong person has the manifest
one phone call will expose the operation
antagonist_answers: the rule of law is worth a life
protecting your own is not a crime
the truth can wait until people are safe

literary.label: Literary Fiction
conventions: Language as a primary pleasure
Interiority with moral weight
Structure that rhymes rather than only escalates
Ambiguity earned by precision
literary.reader_promise: Attention: the reader should feel seen in an unfamiliar life.
pitfalls: Withheld information as a substitute for tension
Ending that explains its own theme
literary.content_notes: Autofiction must not present invented events about real, named people as fact.
settings: a house being emptied after a death
a town with one bus out
a flat above a laundry
a hospital ward at the end of the corridor
pressures: a debt comes due that no one will name
a letter arrives forty years late
the family business is being sold in secret
someone has started returning what they took
antagonist_answers: dignity is a private matter
you owe the dead nothing
leaving is a form of loyalty

historical.label: Historical Fiction
conventions: A documented period with research surfaced as texture
Material constraint that shapes plot
Language that avoids anachronism
A fact/invention ledger
historical.reader_promise: Being there: the past as lived constraint, not costume.
historical.content_notes: Flag every invented historical person or event; never attribute invented words to real figures.
settings: a market town during a bad harvest
a canal junction with one warehouse
a garrison town on a payday
a mill village after the flood
pressures: the tax rolls are being rewritten this quarter
a strike vote is three days away
the parish register has a forged entry
the railway arrives next spring and takes the common
antagonist_answers: the record is how the poor survive
progress will feed more than it starves
obedience is the only safety a woman has

comedy.label: Comedy
conventions: A comic premise with escalating stakes
Specific, character-driven jokes
Callbacks that pay structural debt
Straight man or norm anchor
comedy.reader_promise: Surprise plus recognition: the joke must be true about someone the reader knows.
comedy.content_notes: No humour built on real protected characteristics, real disasters, or real private individuals.
roles: wedding planner for a family business
estate agent for one terrible street
settings: a hotel hosting two rival conferences
a community centre with one working room
a caravan park in a heatwave
a supermarket at 23:00
pressures: two events are booked in the same room at the same hour
the award is being presented to the wrong person
the boss's surprise party has surprise guests
one spreadsheet now controls everyone's weekend
antagonist_answers: competence will be recognised eventually
nobody actually reads the policy
if you never admit fault it never happened

slice-of-life.label: Slice of Life
conventions: Small, concrete stakes
Repetition with variation
Ritual and season
An ensemble that shares a place
slice-of-life.reader_promise: Company: the reader should want to stay in the room after the story ends.
pitfalls: Ending on a list of feelings
settings: a launderette at the end of a bus route
a bakery before the first delivery
a library with one reading room
a riverside allotment in late summer
pressures: the lease is up for renewal in a month
the regular who comes every day has stopped coming
the family recipe book has gone missing
a new shop opens across the road
antagonist_answers: small kindnesses are the whole of it
staying is a choice, not a failure
privacy is a courtesy you owe your neighbours

young-adult.label: Young Adult
conventions: A protagonist with partial agency and real constraints
Adults present but not decisive
Identity stakes felt as survival stakes
A voice the reader would follow anywhere
young-adult.reader_promise: Recognition plus momentum: the reader's present feels consequential.
young-adult.content_notes: No explicit sex; substance use and self-harm depicted without method detail or instruction.
settings: a school with a leaking roof and one good theatre
a town where the factory is closing
a summer job nobody else wanted
a hospital that smells like the person you lost
pressures: the scholarship depends on one exam
the video is already circulating
the move happens in eight weeks
the injury will not heal before the season ends
antagonist_answers: being honest will cost you everything
you owe your family your future
being liked is the same as being safe

cyberpunk.label: Cyberpunk
conventions: Unequal access to bodies, data, and shelter
Corporate power as weather
Street-level competence and slang
Technology that monetizes intimacy
cyberpunk.reader_promise: Systemic anger made personal: the reader should feel the invoice of the future.
pitfalls: Dystopia as backdrop with no cost
cyberpunk.content_notes: No real corporate targets, real exploits, or instructions for intrusion.
roles: debt collector for a housing platform
settings: a tower where rent is charged by the minute
a clinic under a transit viaduct
a market of refurbished implants
a district that loses power at the same hour nightly
pressures: the implant lease is up and the body is not paid off
the district's access tier drops at midnight
a backup has been restored without consent
the platform has priced the water out of reach
antagonist_answers: your body is your last property
the system can be worked from inside
solidarity is the only leverage left

fabulation.label: Fabulation / Magical Realism
conventions: One impossible element accepted as ordinary
Historical or political weight carried by the fantastic
Understatement of the miraculous
Domestic detail that anchors the strange
fabulation.reader_promise: Acceptance: the impossible is treated as a fact of life, and that fact has consequences.
roles: bus driver on a mountain route
settings: a village where the dead are buried twice
a house that keeps every letter ever written in it
a river that changes its course when someone lies
a town that receives rain only at funerals
pressures: the saint's day approaches and no one will perform the ritual
the house has begun returning things taken from it
the water table is falling as the arguments grow
the registry shows a name no living person claims
antagonist_answers: the dead must be fed or they will not stay dead
memory is a communal duty
miracles are ordinary and therefore unremarked
